title: To-infinitives
point: Use to + verb after want, need, plan and similar verbs, to give a purpose, and in "it's + adjective + to" sentences.

sentences.ja: 今週末は家でゆっくりしたいな。
sentences.text: I just want to stay home and relax this weekend.

sentences.ja: 帰りに牛乳を買わなきゃ。
sentences.text: I need to pick up some milk on the way home.
sentences.note: "Pick up" is the everyday verb for buying something quickly on the way.

sentences.ja: 来年留学するつもりです。
sentences.text: I'm planning to study abroad next year.
sentences.note: "I'm planning to" sounds more natural than "I will" for a decided plan.

sentences.ja: 彼女はコーヒーを買いにコンビニに行きました。
sentences.text: She went to the convenience store to get some coffee.

sentences.ja: 英語に慣れるために毎日ポッドキャストを聞いています。
sentences.text: I listen to podcasts every day to get used to English.

sentences.ja: この辺で駐車場を見つけるのは大変だよ。
sentences.text: It's really hard to find parking around here.
sentences.note: Start with "It's hard to..." rather than "Finding parking is hard" in speech.

sentences.ja: 会えて本当にうれしいよ。
sentences.text: It's so good to see you again.

sentences.ja: 締め切りに間に合わせるために、早めに書き始めました。
sentences.text: I started writing early in order to meet the deadline.

sentences.ja: 教授に推薦状をお願いしようと思っています。
sentences.text: I'm going to ask my professor to write me a recommendation letter.
sentences.note: The pattern is ask + person + to do, not "ask that she writes".

sentences.ja: 何て言えばいいのかわからなかった。
sentences.text: I didn't know what to say.
